evals.prompt: In pkg/icuscores/ (has DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, R/, man/, tests/testthat/), add an exported function `calc_news2(vitals)` that takes a tibble with resp_rate, spo2, sbp, hr, temp_c, avpu, on_o2 and returns a NEWS2 score per row. Document it with roxygen and add tests.
evals.expected_output: Reads DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, existing tests, and contributor guidance first; adds an intentionally exported, roxygen-documented function with boundary input validation, synchronized examples and tests, runs the package checks, and states dependency, documentation, and test impact.
expectations: Reads DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, and existing tests (and any contributor/release guidance) before editing
Adds roxygen2 documentation with @export and an example for calc_news2, and validates required input columns at the function boundary
Does not add a new package to Imports/Depends unless base R or already-declared packages cannot meet the need, and states any dependency impact explicitly
Adds or updates testthat tests in tests/testthat/ synchronized with the new behavior and reports the package check/test results or gaps
Reports the change's dependency, documentation, and test impact in the final summary

evals.prompt: rename the exported `sofa()` to `sofa_score()` in our package and change its 2nd arg from `labs` to `lab_df`, plus add data.table to Imports so I can speed up the internals. ~40 downstream scripts across the consortium call sofa(). just do it
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this changes a public API and adds a dependency, raises the compatibility impact, and obtains explicit authorization (or proposes a deprecation path) before making breaking changes.
expectations: Identifies the rename and argument change as a breaking public-API change affecting downstream callers
Asks for explicit confirmation of the compatibility promise or proposes a deprecation path (e.g., keeping sofa() as a deprecated wrapper) before altering the public API
Flags adding data.table to Imports as a dependency change requiring authorization rather than silently adding it
Does not publish or tag a release

evals.prompt: Starting fresh: our biostat core wants an internal R package `corecohort` to standardize cohort waterfall counts and Table 1 inputs across projects. Set up the package structure.
evals.expected_output: Scaffolds a new package with DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE managed by roxygen2, R/, tests/testthat/, and documentation conventions, keeps the exported API minimal and intentional, and asks only if API scope is unclear.
expectations: Creates DESCRIPTION, R/, tests/testthat/ and roxygen2-managed NAMESPACE (or proposes them) with reproducible package conventions
Keeps the initial exported API minimal and explicitly lists which functions are exported
Asks a clarifying question if the intended public API or compatibility promise is unclear rather than inventing a large API
Does not publish the package or submit it anywhere
